--- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.edge_clustering_coefficient()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: Get edge clustering coefficient for specified edges. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.edge_clustering_coefficient()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: Get edge clustering coefficient for specified edges. title: >- [Graph.edge_clustering_coefficient()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: Get edge clustering coefficient for specified edges. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Get edge clustering coefficient for specified edges. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L38212-L38372){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.edge_clustering_coefficient( edge_ids=None, k=3, normalized=True, offset=True, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Edge clustering coefficient](../assets/graphs/edge-clustering-coefficient.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="The shared seven-node graph with edge C-D in accent and the two triangles through it, B-C-D and C-D-E, shaded. With endpoint degrees 4 and 3 at most 2 triangles are possible, so the default score is (2 + 1) / 2 = 1.5, shown in the card." width="100%"} The edge clustering coefficient measures how "clustered" the neighborhood around an edge is, based on k-cycles (cycles of length k) the edge participates in. For `k=3` (triangles): - counts triangles containing the edge - maximum possible: `min(d_i - 1, d_j - 1)` where `d_i`, `d_j` are endpoint degrees - value of `1.0` means edge is in a complete subgraph For `k=4` (4-cycles): - counts 4-cycles containing the edge - maximum possible: `(d_i - 1)(d_j - 1)` - measures "squareness" of edge neighborhood Where node clustering asks how tightly a node's neighbors are linked, this metric asks the same question of an edge. Edges inside a dense group take part in many short cycles and score high; edges that bridge two groups take part in few or none and score low. That makes the measure useful for: - finding bridge-like edges that connect otherwise separate communities - divisive community detection (repeatedly removing the lowest-scoring edge, as in Radicchi et al., 2004) - judging the strength of ties in social networks, where embedded ties tend to be strong Edges with an endpoint of degree 1 cannot be in any cycle and always score `0.0` when `normalized=True` (even with `offset=True`), because the maximum possible count is zero. The measure is defined for undirected graphs; on a directed graph, cycles are found by following outgoing edges only, which is rarely what you want, so consider converting with `to_undirected()` first. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [edge_ids]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[int] | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : List of edge IDs (integers) to compute the coefficient for. Edge IDs can be read from the `id` column of `get_edge_df()`. IDs that do not match any edge are silently ignored. If `None` (default), computes for all edges. [k]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[3]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Cycle size to use. Must be `3` (default, triangles) or `4` (4-cycles); any other value raises a `ValueError`. Triangles capture the usual notion of clustering; 4-cycles are informative in graphs that have few triangles by construction, such as bipartite graphs or grids. [normalized]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether to normalize by maximum possible cycles given endpoint degrees. If `True` (default), the (possibly offset) cycle count is divided by the maximum shown above. If `False`, returns the raw cycle count (plus `1` if `offset=` is `True`). [offset]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether to add `1` to cycle count (original Radicchi et al. definition). When `offset=True` (default): `C(e) = (z + 1) / s`. When `offset=False`: `C(e) = z / s`. The offset keeps edges in zero cycles from being tied at `0` (except those with a degree-1 endpoint, which stay at `0`), but it also lets scores exceed `1`. Use `offset=False` when you want an interpretable `[0, 1]` proportion. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [dict[int, float]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Mapping from edge ID (integer) to clustering coefficient, with one entry for each requested edge that exists. With `normalized=True`: range `[0, 1]` when `offset=False` and up to `2` when `offset=True`. With `normalized=False`: raw cycle count (plus `1` if `offset=True`). ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `k=` is not `3` or `4`. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Radicchi et al. (2004) introduced this metric to identify community-bridging edges: edges embedded in many short cycles are internal to a community, while those embedded in few are candidates for removal in Girvan-Newman-style algorithms. Their original definition uses `normalized=True` and `offset=True`, which adds $1$ to the raw cycle count so a score of $0$ never appears (other than for edges with a degree-1 endpoint); setting `offset=False` recovers the more natural convention where an edge inside a complete subgraph scores exactly $1$. Runtime is $O(|V|\,d\log d + |E|\,d)$ for $k=3$ (triangles) and $O(|V|\,d\log d + |E|\,d^2)$ for $k=4$ (4-cycles), where $d$ is the maximum degree. ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~local_clustering_coefficient`) : Clustering of each node. [](`~generalized_degree`) : Each node's edges by how many triangles they lie in. [](`~edge_betweenness_centrality`) : Find the edges that many shortest paths cross. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Two triangles are joined by the edge `C`-`D`, which lies in no triangle. With the default `offset=True`, each score is one more than the edge's triangles, divided by the most it could have, so the joining edge scores `(0 + 1) / 2` and the others `(1 + 1) / 1`: ::: {#8af67c39 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph.from_edges( [("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "A"), ("C", "D"), ("D", "E"), ("E", "F"), ("F", "D")] ) scores = graph.edge_clustering_coefficient() graph.set_edge_attrs("clustering", scores) graph.get_edge_df(labels=True).select("source", "target", "clustering") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ```{=html}

With `k=4`, the score counts squares instead of triangles: ::: {#053999a8 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} square = ec.Graph().add_cycle_graph(4) square.edge_clustering_coefficient(offset=False, k=4) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` {3: 1.0, 1: 1.0, 4: 1.0, 2: 1.0} ``` ::: ::: ### Weak ties between the factions `karate_club()` links the 34 members of a university karate club who met outside the club, before it split in two. Of the 78 friendships, the six lowest-scoring are member `11`'s only friendship and five of the ten that cross between the factions: ::: {#c7e18ac6 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} karate = ec.karate_club() karate.set_edge_attrs("clustering", karate.edge_clustering_coefficient()) ( karate.get_edge_df(labels=True) .sort("clustering") .select("source", "target", "clustering") .head(6) ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}
